Lock In Your Home’s Summer Exterior Painting Makeover Now
May 28, 2025
Lock In Your Home’s Summer Exterior Painting Makeover Now

A home’s exterior is about more than just its walls. The trim, siding, shutters, gutters, decks, fascia boards, and more must stand up to the elements all year, too. Eventually, however, battle scars appear in the form of faded colors and chipped paint, calling for a professional paint job. 




Your house may need repainting anywhere from every three to 20 years, depending on the materials, the quality of the previous paint job, any existing damage, and Washington’s climate. 




Timing is also everything, and summer is prime time for these projects! 




At EA Pro Painters, the top-rated painting company in Washington, we believe you should lock in your rates and time for a summer exterior house painting before we’re booked. Let’s tell you why. 




Summer and Exterior Painting in Washington
 

Every summer in Washington, the clouds of spring part ways for sunshine, blue skies, and golden afternoons. By mid-June, the state officially shakes off the rainy season, giving people a much-needed window of good weather! It’s hands-down the time for exterior painting. 




Warm Weather 




A good paint job starts long before the first brushstroke — it begins with prep, which involves the following: 




Washing: A clean surface is a must for proper paint adhesion, and it reveals any damage. Get rid of dust, mildew, pollen, and other debris. 
Repairing: After cleaning the surface, fix cracks, holes, or rotted wood. The goal is to have a sound structure and a smooth finish. 
Scraping: Scraping removes any loose or peeling paint from the surface using tools like putty knives. 
Sanding: Once scraping is complete, sand to even out the surface, feather out rough edges, and roughen glossy areas. 
Priming: Priming seals porous surfaces, covers repairs, and creates a uniform base for the final coats of paint. Primer also extends the life of your paint job. 

For all these steps to be effective, the surface should be dry. Otherwise, the paint won’t bond and may peel, crack, or blister. 




Summer weather then shines, literally and figuratively. It brings just the right warmth to ensure surfaces, primer, and paint are moisture-free. Moreover, painters don’t have to worry about the paint drying too quickly (leaving visible brush marks) or not drying at all! 




Small Chances of Rain 




A surprise shower can ruin fresh paint, leave streaks, and drag out the timeline of your project. Fortunately, early to mid-summer in Washington is all about crisp weather! 




Of course, no season is entirely rain-free, but having your project underway during this optimal window lowers the risk of weather-related delays. Experienced crews like EA Pro Painters always watch the forecast closely. Count on us to plan the most workable painting schedule. 




Long Days 




Summer gives you the gift of extra daylight. With the sun rising early and setting late, painters can work on more square footage in a day, meaning they can finish the project faster. 




Natural light is also pivotal to the painting process, allowing for better visibility. You get more accurate color matching and the ability to spot touch-ups or imperfections that artificial lighting might not reveal. 




Steady Temperatures 




Too much variation can prevent paint from curing properly. As such, exterior paint thrives under consistent conditions. 




In summer, you can expect more stable, predictable temperatures than in other seasons, steering clear of durability woes! How does the season in Washington look in degrees? 




Western Washington: Summer temperatures rarely climb above 79°F, with the Pacific Ocean cooling things down. 
Eastern Washington: Higher summer temperatures, usually in the upper 80s to mid-90s, still fall within the paint-friendly range. 

Protection From Extreme Heat 




Paint is decorative and protective. It becomes a barrier against moisture, UV rays, and pest intrusion when applied correctly. Painting in the summer means you’re giving your house a head start on defense. 




A freshly painted exterior also helps regulate indoor temperatures by lessening heat transfer through your walls. That extra insulation? Your respite on late summer’s hottest days! Pull your cooling costs down and keep your household comfortable. 




Enhanced Curb Appeal 




What is summer, if not a time to show off your space? With Washington welcoming millions of tourists annually during this season, curb appeal counts more than ever! 




Host a backyard BBQ, welcome guests from out of town, or simply enjoy quiet nights on the porch; a newly painted abode stands out and signals pride of ownership. 




For homeowners thinking of selling in the future, painting is a practical way to boost value. And even if you’re staying put, there’s nothing quite like pulling into your driveway and seeing a home that looks brand new again. 




EA Pro Painters’ Exterior Painting Services 



Painting your property’s exterior maintains its structural integrity and long-term worth. It’s an investment, especially when you let local professionals take over. 




At EA Pro Painters, we specialize in comprehensive exterior painting services in Washington, eager to make every dwelling across the state beautiful and protected. What can our team of experts do for you? 




Fresh Exterior Painting 




Congratulations on your new house! Let’s turn it into an even more breathtaking one with a top-tier exterior painting. We use advanced techniques and the highest quality materials to defend against moisture, sun, and time. 




Exterior Repainting 




Sometimes, houses just need a refresh. Maybe you don’t want to see all those peeling and fading, or perhaps you’re ready for a new color. Whatever your reason, our painters will have the brushes on your walls in no time! 




Siding Painting 




Painting siding materials like vinyl or aluminum is a specialty job, and one EA Pro Painters has perfected. We know the best prep methods and coatings! Our team is available for inspections and consultations so we can decide on the hues and finishes together. 




Wood Staining 




We love residences with natural wood features and preserve them through expert staining services. Bring out the grain’s charm while shielding it from UV rays, moisture, and general wear! We use only premium stains, promising durability and style. 




Brick Painting and Limewashing 




Brick is classic, but that doesn’t mean you can’t enhance it. You can go for a modern painted look or a soft, old-world feel with limewash. Our treatments allow the natural texture to shine through and keep erosion and other possible damage at bay. 




Why Book EA Pro Painters Before Summer? 



Summer is the most suitable time for exterior painting projects. Should you wait until it arrives to book EA Pro Painters? Nope! By the time the sunny days hit, our calendar is usually packed. 




EA Pro Painters is proud to be one of the most trusted painting companies on the Eastside of the greater Seattle area. We’ve transformed properties in Bellevue, Redmond, Kirkland, Sammamish, Issaquah, Bothell, Woodinville, Duvall, Factoria, and beyond, offering honesty, integrity, and quality craftsmanship to the communities. 




That said, we never just apply a coat of paint and move on. Our team brings years of hands-on experience to every job! And because we commit to doing every job right and not rushing, we don’t overbook during summer. 




We limit the number of projects we take on to keep the exacting standards our clients expect. If you wait too long, you may miss your chance to have us onboard. We don’t want that to happen, either! 




Perks of Locking in Your Rate and Date Now 




Again, lock in your rates and time for a summer exterior house painting before we’re booked up. Here’s what you gain by scheduling your project now: 




Sufficient Time for Preparation: With dedicated days for your project, we get ample time to prep the surfaces we’ll be working on thoroughly and properly. Don’t worry; your only duty is to remove outdoor decorations and cover delicate plants. We’ll take care of everything else! 
Good Deals: EA Pro Painters offers excellent value all year round. Since summer is peak season for painting, we have special rates you can snag! Moreover, knowing your estimate beforehand will allow you to plan your finances. We don’t do last-minute surprises — just premium service priced with transparency. 
Guaranteed Visual Perfection and Design Precision: Are you dreaming of a fresh neutral tone or a bold pop of color? Tell us, and we’ll realize it. We communicate every step of the way, listen to your goals, and focus on results that last. Book us early so we can dedicate the time and attention you and your property deserve. 

Here’s a bonus: All our work is warranty-protected for four years. That’s how much we want to assure you and trust our services! 




Get a Rate and Schedule Now 




Every homeowner wants their living spaces to be at their best. The easiest, most transformative upgrade you can invest in? Exterior painting! 




In Washington, summers have the ideal conditions for this project. With neighbors thinking the same, you must get yours on the schedule before they do. If you live in Washington’s Eastside, EA Pro Painters is the name to rely on. 




We’re ready for the season to inspire makeovers, especially in your home, starting from the outside. Lock in your rates and time for a summer exterior house painting before we’re booked solid! 




Call EA Pro Painters at (206) 250-1194 or contact us online.

 How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Your Home in 2025 
 May 14, 2025 
 How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Your Home in 2025  
 Nothing compares to the feeling of building a new house or refreshing an old one. The process can be exciting, with anticipation and stress playing in equal measure. After all, shaping a space that hinges on style, needs, and aspirations is not a game! Now, if there is one aspect that wraps up your residential project, it is the exterior. The outside of your home is what makes its first impression. As such, choosing a paint color is a decision every homeowner should consider carefully. What color should you use? At EA Pro Painters, we can teach you how to choose the best paint colors for exterior painting in 2025.  2025 Home Color Trends  
Your decisions about exterior paint are more important than you might think. You do not just apply a color; you make it fit your vision, lifestyle, local climate, neighborhood, and everything else. Exterior painting sets the tone for what is inside your house and has the power to elevate it. Your home may stand out in your community or blend with it. Aesthetics aside, the paint will also protect your house for decades. So, should you go bold and be daring or pick something timeless and classic? Perhaps the design trends for 2025 can point you toward the perfect answer.  Earth Tones  
More homeowners are gravitating toward natural, earthy tones. Shades of brown and green? People are falling in love with them! Experts say this shift results from the desire for warmth and authenticity in home design. These colors make a house look and feel lived-in, cozy, and deeply connected to its environment, which many want. Earth tones include ivory, soft and navy blue, dusty pink, and sage green. You can also explore crimson reds, terracotta, and charcoal gray. Anything that reminds you of the beauty of nature falls under this trend.  Dark Color Palettes... with Nuance  
Have you ever seen a black house? It is no longer as uncommon as it used to be, but it can still feel quite refreshing in the sense that it differs from the usual colors. For 2025, darker colors like black, charcoal gray, and navy blue go with brighter tones, such as beige and cream. There is something about rich shades and lighter, airy hues that create an interesting contrast and add nuance. You can balance boldness and modernity with softness and sophistication. And it is hard not to want it for your own home.  Vibrant Colors  
Yes, calm, earthy tones and deep dark shades are in, but energetic colors are also gathering many fans. Homeowners are saying yes to bright yellows, oranges, and teals, which are undeniably dynamic and eye-catching! Vivid colors make a house pop; they define “fun,” “funky,” and “adventurous.” This trend proves we are over the longstanding gray-and-white, safe color schemes, and that it is time to be loud and proud. If those adjectives resonate with your vision, then splashing your exterior with lively hues should be on your agenda.  2025 Popular Palettes to Check Out  
EA Pro Painters, the leading painting company in the greater Eastside area of King County, always tracks the color trends of each year. How home design jumps from one vogue to another fascinates us, and we help homeowners make decisions based on all factors. When it comes to exterior painting, our team caught two palettes that stand out in 2025. Check them out to see if they are “the one” for you.  Benjamin Moore’s Cinnamon Slate  
Premium paints and stains are Benjamin Moore’s gift to the painting industry. The brand produces resins and proprietary Gennex® colorants, setting the industry standard for excellence since 1883. Consequently, you can trust its extensive selection of authentic, carefully crafted colors and paints formulated to deliver beautiful, long-lasting results. Benjamin Moore’s Color of the Year for 2025 is Cinnamon Slate. It is both heathered plum and velvety brown, and every house it graces exudes a certain refinement. Expect your home to feel grounded. Cinnamon Slate shares a harmonious bond with Mink Violet, Vintage Charm, Frozen in Time, and Bonne Nuit. To complete your palette, pair it with Cloud Cover, Porcelain, Calm, or Chambord. For more experimentation, explore shades like Antique Pearl, Mauve Desert, Bison Brown, Pinecone Brown, and Chocolate Sundae. Imagine the layered look these hues can create!  Sherwin-Williams Color Capsule  
Sherwin-Williams boasts one of the most renowned portfolios of both branded and private-label products. Its exclusive products are only available through a network of more than 5,000 company-operated shops and facilities in the United States, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America. Their 2025 Color Capsule of the Year features the following:  Grounded: A versatile brown from the 2025 Colormix® Forecast “enveloping” spaces in a calming nature. Sun bleached: This color sits between warm and cool tones, deeper than white but not quite gray, and hints of beige or taupe. Chartreuse: A vibrant yellow green that brings a joyful, tropical brightness with a burst of energy. Rain Cloud: This stormy, deep gray-blue bridges classic design with contemporary updates. Clove: Clove is nearly black and entrancing brown, ideal for the most intimate spaces. Malabar: This soft, sandy beige neutral is a perfect base for layering with delicate, warm hues. Bosc Pear: A luxurious gold that shifts toward organic, luxe tones kindling nostalgia. White Snow: A pure, brilliantly bright white with a light reflectance value of 90 for crisp, clean homes. Mauve Finery: Mauve Finery is a subdued hue that evokes botanical beauty and brings a dreamy quality to homes.  
 How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Exterior Painting  
We have shared many clues to guide you in your residential exterior painting project. If you still have not landed on the perfect color, no worries. It 
should take a lot of back and forth! Moreover, taking your time is better than rushing into unfitting hues. We will not leave you hanging, of course. Here are eight expert tips on how to choose the best paint colors for exterior painting.  Look at Your Neighborhood  
Walk around your neighborhood to learn its vibe. What colors are the other homes? Decide if you want to contribute to the area’s cohesive aesthetics or stand out. A good concept is to fit in but not get lost, and there is always a color to achieve that.  Observe Your Surroundings  
What surrounds your house is also vital, so look at the trees, plants, and elements around you. You can paint according to your surroundings or make the surroundings work for you. If you live in a forested area, earthy tones might feel like a natural extension. In contrast, hues of the sky and sand will do well if you live in a coastal or desert community.  Think About the Local Climate  
If you live in a sunny climate, lighter colors will reflect the sun’s rays and keep your living spaces cooler. On the other hand, darker colors absorb heat, giving your house a warmer feel. Yes, your paint color will also interact with the weather, especially in terms of durability and maintenance. Factor that in, too.  Evaluate Your House’s Architectural Style  
Traditional homes often become stunning in classic hues, while modern ones benefit from bolder choices. Does your house have historic features? You might want to stick to period-appropriate colors that preserve its charm. Generally, your exterior color improves the architectural design rather than competing with it.  Assess Your Building Materials  
Whether your house is made of brick, wood, stucco, or stone, the texture and inherent color of the building materials will affect how the coat of paint looks. For instance, red bricks pair well with creamy whites. Wooden homes, especially those with abundant natural grain, will need earthy tones or dark stains to highlight the wood’s beauty. Ask experts about this part to ensure you get a visually appealing result.  Consider Your Interiors  
Exterior and interior design are two different worlds, but your home is a 
unified space. What works on the outside 
should flow to the inside. If you already have interior color palettes, go for exterior colors that align with them. It is possible to have varying color schemes, but they should not veer too far off, or you get a disoriented effect.  Test Swatches  
Once you have a shortlist of colors, never rely on small paint chips from the store. A color might appear different when applied to the exterior versus on a sample card. Paint larger test swatches directly on the exterior of your house and see the color in various lighting throughout the day. This practice will give you the most accurate sense of how the color will work in your space.  Pick a Palette  
Have you narrowed down your choices? Move on to a full palette of complementary shades! Exterior colors are best when layered; have a main color for the body, a trim color for architectural features, and an accent color for doors, shutters, or other focal points. Balance light and dark tones for depth and visual interest.  Let Us Help You with Your Residential Exterior Painting  
When you are at the exterior painting phase of your project, EA Pro Painters wants to help you make the most of it. Visit our shop in Factoria near Bellevue, Washington, to talk to our team of experts. We are also next to a Sherwin-Williams store, and we can accompany you as you choose your colors. Until your house looks and feels like a home, EA Pro Painters will be with you every step of the way. Call (206) 250-1194 or 
contact us online today!

How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Your Home in 2025
May 14, 2025
How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Your Home in 2025 

Nothing compares to the feeling of building a new house or refreshing an old one. The process can be exciting, with anticipation and stress playing in equal measure. After all, shaping a space that hinges on style, needs, and aspirations is not a game! 




Now, if there is one aspect that wraps up your residential project, it is the exterior. The outside of your home is what makes its first impression. As such, choosing a paint color is a decision every homeowner should consider carefully. 




What color should you use? At EA Pro Painters, we can teach you how to choose the best paint colors for exterior painting in 2025. 




2025 Home Color Trends 




Your decisions about exterior paint are more important than you might think. You do not just apply a color; you make it fit your vision, lifestyle, local climate, neighborhood, and everything else. 




Exterior painting sets the tone for what is inside your house and has the power to elevate it. Your home may stand out in your community or blend with it. Aesthetics aside, the paint will also protect your house for decades. 




So, should you go bold and be daring or pick something timeless and classic? Perhaps the design trends for 2025 can point you toward the perfect answer. 




Earth Tones 




More homeowners are gravitating toward natural, earthy tones. Shades of brown and green? People are falling in love with them! Experts say this shift results from the desire for warmth and authenticity in home design. These colors make a house look and feel lived-in, cozy, and deeply connected to its environment, which many want. 




Earth tones include ivory, soft and navy blue, dusty pink, and sage green. You can also explore crimson reds, terracotta, and charcoal gray. Anything that reminds you of the beauty of nature falls under this trend. 




Dark Color Palettes... with Nuance 




Have you ever seen a black house? It is no longer as uncommon as it used to be, but it can still feel quite refreshing in the sense that it differs from the usual colors. 




For 2025, darker colors like black, charcoal gray, and navy blue go with brighter tones, such as beige and cream. There is something about rich shades and lighter, airy hues that create an interesting contrast and add nuance. You can balance boldness and modernity with softness and sophistication. And it is hard not to want it for your own home. 




Vibrant Colors 




Yes, calm, earthy tones and deep dark shades are in, but energetic colors are also gathering many fans. Homeowners are saying yes to bright yellows, oranges, and teals, which are undeniably dynamic and eye-catching! 




Vivid colors make a house pop; they define “fun,” “funky,” and “adventurous.” This trend proves we are over the longstanding gray-and-white, safe color schemes, and that it is time to be loud and proud. If those adjectives resonate with your vision, then splashing your exterior with lively hues should be on your agenda. 




2025 Popular Palettes to Check Out 



EA Pro Painters, the leading painting company in the greater Eastside area of King County, always tracks the color trends of each year. How home design jumps from one vogue to another fascinates us, and we help homeowners make decisions based on all factors. 




When it comes to exterior painting, our team caught two palettes that stand out in 2025. Check them out to see if they are “the one” for you. 




Benjamin Moore’s Cinnamon Slate 




Premium paints and stains are Benjamin Moore’s gift to the painting industry. The brand produces resins and proprietary Gennex® colorants, setting the industry standard for excellence since 1883. Consequently, you can trust its extensive selection of authentic, carefully crafted colors and paints formulated to deliver beautiful, long-lasting results. 




Benjamin Moore’s Color of the Year for 2025 is Cinnamon Slate. It is both heathered plum and velvety brown, and every house it graces exudes a certain refinement. Expect your home to feel grounded. 




Cinnamon Slate shares a harmonious bond with Mink Violet, Vintage Charm, Frozen in Time, and Bonne Nuit. To complete your palette, pair it with Cloud Cover, Porcelain, Calm, or Chambord. For more experimentation, explore shades like Antique Pearl, Mauve Desert, Bison Brown, Pinecone Brown, and Chocolate Sundae. Imagine the layered look these hues can create! 




Sherwin-Williams Color Capsule 




Sherwin-Williams boasts one of the most renowned portfolios of both branded and private-label products. Its exclusive products are only available through a network of more than 5,000 company-operated shops and facilities in the United States, Canada, the Caribbean, and Latin America. Their 2025 Color Capsule of the Year features the following: 




Grounded: A versatile brown from the 2025 Colormix® Forecast “enveloping” spaces in a calming nature. 
Sun bleached: This color sits between warm and cool tones, deeper than white but not quite gray, and hints of beige or taupe. 
Chartreuse: A vibrant yellow green that brings a joyful, tropical brightness with a burst of energy. 
Rain Cloud: This stormy, deep gray-blue bridges classic design with contemporary updates. 
Clove: Clove is nearly black and entrancing brown, ideal for the most intimate spaces. 
Malabar: This soft, sandy beige neutral is a perfect base for layering with delicate, warm hues. 
Bosc Pear: A luxurious gold that shifts toward organic, luxe tones kindling nostalgia. 
White Snow: A pure, brilliantly bright white with a light reflectance value of 90 for crisp, clean homes. 
Mauve Finery: Mauve Finery is a subdued hue that evokes botanical beauty and brings a dreamy quality to homes. 




How To Choose the Best Paint Colors for Exterior Painting 



We have shared many clues to guide you in your residential exterior painting project. If you still have not landed on the perfect color, no worries. It should take a lot of back and forth! Moreover, taking your time is better than rushing into unfitting hues. 




We will not leave you hanging, of course. Here are eight expert tips on how to choose the best paint colors for exterior painting. 




Look at Your Neighborhood 




Walk around your neighborhood to learn its vibe. What colors are the other homes? Decide if you want to contribute to the area’s cohesive aesthetics or stand out. A good concept is to fit in but not get lost, and there is always a color to achieve that. 




Observe Your Surroundings 




What surrounds your house is also vital, so look at the trees, plants, and elements around you. You can paint according to your surroundings or make the surroundings work for you. If you live in a forested area, earthy tones might feel like a natural extension. In contrast, hues of the sky and sand will do well if you live in a coastal or desert community. 




Think About the Local Climate 




If you live in a sunny climate, lighter colors will reflect the sun’s rays and keep your living spaces cooler. On the other hand, darker colors absorb heat, giving your house a warmer feel. Yes, your paint color will also interact with the weather, especially in terms of durability and maintenance. Factor that in, too. 




Evaluate Your House’s Architectural Style 




Traditional homes often become stunning in classic hues, while modern ones benefit from bolder choices. Does your house have historic features? You might want to stick to period-appropriate colors that preserve its charm. Generally, your exterior color improves the architectural design rather than competing with it. 




Assess Your Building Materials 




Whether your house is made of brick, wood, stucco, or stone, the texture and inherent color of the building materials will affect how the coat of paint looks. For instance, red bricks pair well with creamy whites. Wooden homes, especially those with abundant natural grain, will need earthy tones or dark stains to highlight the wood’s beauty. Ask experts about this part to ensure you get a visually appealing result. 




Consider Your Interiors 




Exterior and interior design are two different worlds, but your home is a unified space. What works on the outside should flow to the inside. If you already have interior color palettes, go for exterior colors that align with them. It is possible to have varying color schemes, but they should not veer too far off, or you get a disoriented effect. 




Test Swatches 




Once you have a shortlist of colors, never rely on small paint chips from the store. A color might appear different when applied to the exterior versus on a sample card. Paint larger test swatches directly on the exterior of your house and see the color in various lighting throughout the day. This practice will give you the most accurate sense of how the color will work in your space. 




Pick a Palette 




Have you narrowed down your choices? Move on to a full palette of complementary shades! Exterior colors are best when layered; have a main color for the body, a trim color for architectural features, and an accent color for doors, shutters, or other focal points. Balance light and dark tones for depth and visual interest. 




Let Us Help You with Your Residential Exterior Painting 



When you are at the exterior painting phase of your project, EA Pro Painters wants to help you make the most of it. Visit our shop in Factoria near Bellevue, Washington, to talk to our team of experts. We are also next to a Sherwin-Williams store, and we can accompany you as you choose your colors. 




Until your house looks and feels like a home, EA Pro Painters will be with you every step of the way. Call (206) 250-1194 or contact us online today!

 Deck Staining vs. Painting: Which Is Best for Your Outdoor Space? 
 May 13, 2025 
 Deck Staining vs. Painting 
 Living in Washington has many benefits — access to nature despite being in a big city, countless job opportunities, and entertainment and culture always just around the corner. As a homeowner in the state, life is almost ideal. But there is 
one 
challenge that can make life a little tricky… Washington’s diverse climate and geography. The western side of the state has relatively mild weather, while the eastern region has more extreme temperatures. If your home isn’t built to withstand natural elements, you won’t be able to make the most of it. A deck, for example, is an exceptional area to revel in Washington’s beauty. To keep it in good condition all year, however, staining or painting is a must. The two differ in application, customizability, cost, and durability, but both aim to protect your outdoor space. In the deck staining vs deck painting debate, which one should you invest in? EA Pro Painters has the answer.  Why Stain or Paint Your Deck?  
Before you choose between deck painting and staining, understand the purpose first. Each method promises different results, but they share the same goal.  Enhance Aesthetics  
Again, outdoor living spaces are for soaking in Washington life; your deck itself should look attractive. Staining and painting can bring out the charm of the materials, whether wood, composite, or PVC. It also boosts your home’s curb appeal with hues that suit the overall architectural design. You live in a welcoming, stylish state, so why not have a deck that reflects that?  Promote Safety  
The deck is where you entertain guests or relax with your family. Along with Washington’s damp and humid climate is regular exposure to moisture, creating slippery surfaces, fostering mold and mildew growth, or deteriorating materials. Stain or paint for a deck safe for foot traffic. These coatings provide a durable, protective surface that eliminates hazards! Consider the primary weather conditions in your area, from high humidity and heavy rainfall to mild temperatures. There is a deck stain or paint to reduce the likelihood of accidents in your home.  Extend Deck Lifespan  
Staining or painting fights moisture, UV rays, fluctuating temperatures, and other natural elements that can lead to rotting, cracking, and other damage. Consequently, your deck serves you well 
longer. Both staining and painting are maintenance tasks that preserve your outdoor space’s integrity, saving you from expensive repairs or replacements.  All About Deck Staining  
Now, let’s round back to the deck staining vs deck painting discourse, starting with the former. Deck staining involves applying a specially formulated stain to your decking materials, penetrating the surface. Transparent stains let the natural wood grain show, while semi-transparent and solid stains offer more color and coverage. Stains form a protective barrier that prevents water from soaking into the materials, avoiding swelling, warping, and rotting. Some also have mildew-resistant properties for more moisture-related issues. Staining also involves UV-blocking agents that safeguard materials from sun damage and does not typically result in peeling or cracking as paint can.  The Pros  
Deck staining comes with several advantages, including the following: Easy to Apply: Stain typically goes on smoothly, not requiring much precision. It is less likely to drip or streak, making it an exciting choice for DIY enthusiasts. Needs Only One Coat: 
 One coat of stain is usually enough to reap the benefits. Budget-Friendly: 
 The materials and tools for staining are more affordable than those for painting. Highlights Wood’s Natural Beauty: Staining preserves and highlights the beauty of the wood, from cedar and redwood to teak.  The Cons  
There are drawbacks to consider before staining, such as the following: Fading Fast in Sunlight: UV rays eventually break down the stain, causing it to lose its vibrant color and finish. Requires Reapplication: 
 Wear and tear can degrade stains faster than paint, so more frequent reapplication may be necessary. Less Variety: The range of stain colors and finishes is generally more limited compared to paints.  In Summary  
Deck staining is ideal for Washington homeowners who want to focus on the allure of wood. For instance, if your deck is made of redwood, it can be impossible to want to cover up its rich, warm reddish-brown hues. The straight and fine grains with knots and swirls are also a stunning visual texture. You must not mind sanding, however. Staining a deck means losing just a bit of the natural wood for aesthetics and resilience. If your deck is placed in an area where the sun doesn’t shine for long each day, staining can be enough. Sunlight is staining’s weakness; with it in shorter supply, your deck will not sustain much damage.  The Power of Deck Painting  
Moving on to the latter part of the deck staining vs deck painting battle, Washington homeowners have even more factors to think about. Deck painting involves applying a layer of paint to the surface of your deck, creating a solid, opaque finish that completely covers it. You can go for oil-based, acrylic, latex, or epoxy paint, based on the level of maintenance you are willing to carry out. Unlike stains, which go through the decking material, paint sits on top. As such, your deck gets a more robust shield against rot, discoloration, and wear. Paint can also help prevent splinters, with a smooth, even surface for walking and furniture placement. Painted decks dramatically transform outdoor spaces. They are not subtle at all, but they are easy to clean, ending the worries that come with wood’s inherent dirt-catching tendencies.  The Pros  
Why should you choose deck painting over staining? Here are four reasons: Long-Lasting: 
 When applied correctly, paint can last several years before requiring touch-ups or reapplication. Excellent UV Light Protection: Paint decreases the risk of the wood fading or turning gray because of exposure to sunlight. Multiple Color and Finish Options: 
 Whether you prefer bold, vibrant colors or lighter shades, paint has a versatility that stains cannot match. You can also choose from satin, matte, or glossy finishes. Better Coverage for Imperfections: Paint hides cracks, blemishes, and age-related wear very well under its layers. The Cons Here are some potential downsides to using paint: More Expensive Than Staining: High-quality exterior paints can be pricey, and you must do more preparation and apply more coats. Maintenance can also be costlier to avoid peeling or chipping. Works Best with Professional Service: Proper preparation and application are pivotal for achieving the best results. Requires Specific Paint: 
 Decks require exterior-grade paints specifically designed for the materials you are using. In Summary Perhaps your house is all red bricks, and you crave a shock of all-white, or maybe you have a pool and want to match its cool blue. Deck painting is the only way to go. The color of your wood might be astonishing, but if it does not match the rest of your property or your taste, painting over it will give you exactly what you visualize. The same solution goes for decks with rough wood surfaces. If staining seeps into cracks and crevices, painting reshapes them in some ways. It hides any unevenness that may be an eyesore. Your deck could be in an area where the sun beats down on it all day or one that cannot avoid rain. Regardless, the paint will shield it.  Deck Staining vs Deck Painting: The Verdict  
With the above perks and pitfalls, it’s easy to see why the deck staining vs deck painting debate has been going on forever. At EA Pro Painters, however, we have a clear winner that we are happy to share with you. Deck staining has its place in home improvement, restoration, and other projects, but painting is one step ahead. It has a higher initial price tag, but it certainly delivers. Aside from preserving that natural wood look, painting can generally do everything staining does — and even better. Deck painting takes a bit more time and effort, but the results speak for themselves. Plus, with proper upkeep, the investment pays off. At the end of the day, a natural, rustic deck is desirable, but it will not matter if it does not last. For superior protection, more aesthetic flexibility, and greater durability, go for deck painting.  Hire EA Pro Painters for Your Next Decking Project  
EA Pro Painters can provide both deck painting and staining. After all, every house and homeowner in Washington has unique needs. Count on our team to assess your deck and decide which finish it should get, merging your budget and preferences with our expertise. As an accredited painting company in the greater Eastside area of King County, we specialize in painting and staining services. Trust us when we say every residence we step into receives professional treatment and the highest quality work. Are you ready to get your deck staining or painting project underway? It could be a new construction or a renovation; either way, EA Pro Painters is eager to be on board. Call (206) 250-1194 now or 
contact us online!

Deck Staining vs. Painting: Which Is Best for Your Outdoor Space?
May 13, 2025
Deck Staining vs. Painting




Living in Washington has many benefits — access to nature despite being in a big city, countless job opportunities, and entertainment and culture always just around the corner. As a homeowner in the state, life is almost ideal. But there is one challenge that can make life a little tricky… Washington’s diverse climate and geography. 




The western side of the state has relatively mild weather, while the eastern region has more extreme temperatures. If your home isn’t built to withstand natural elements, you won’t be able to make the most of it. 




A deck, for example, is an exceptional area to revel in Washington’s beauty. To keep it in good condition all year, however, staining or painting is a must. The two differ in application, customizability, cost, and durability, but both aim to protect your outdoor space. 




In the deck staining vs deck painting debate, which one should you invest in? EA Pro Painters has the answer. 




Why Stain or Paint Your Deck? 



Before you choose between deck painting and staining, understand the purpose first. Each method promises different results, but they share the same goal. 




Enhance Aesthetics 




Again, outdoor living spaces are for soaking in Washington life; your deck itself should look attractive. Staining and painting can bring out the charm of the materials, whether wood, composite, or PVC. It also boosts your home’s curb appeal with hues that suit the overall architectural design. You live in a welcoming, stylish state, so why not have a deck that reflects that? 




Promote Safety 




The deck is where you entertain guests or relax with your family. Along with Washington’s damp and humid climate is regular exposure to moisture, creating slippery surfaces, fostering mold and mildew growth, or deteriorating materials. 




Stain or paint for a deck safe for foot traffic. These coatings provide a durable, protective surface that eliminates hazards! Consider the primary weather conditions in your area, from high humidity and heavy rainfall to mild temperatures. There is a deck stain or paint to reduce the likelihood of accidents in your home. 




Extend Deck Lifespan 




Staining or painting fights moisture, UV rays, fluctuating temperatures, and other natural elements that can lead to rotting, cracking, and other damage. Consequently, your deck serves you well longer. Both staining and painting are maintenance tasks that preserve your outdoor space’s integrity, saving you from expensive repairs or replacements. 




All About Deck Staining 



Now, let’s round back to the deck staining vs deck painting discourse, starting with the former. Deck staining involves applying a specially formulated stain to your decking materials, penetrating the surface. Transparent stains let the natural wood grain show, while semi-transparent and solid stains offer more color and coverage. 




Stains form a protective barrier that prevents water from soaking into the materials, avoiding swelling, warping, and rotting. Some also have mildew-resistant properties for more moisture-related issues. 




Staining also involves UV-blocking agents that safeguard materials from sun damage and does not typically result in peeling or cracking as paint can. 




The Pros 




Deck staining comes with several advantages, including the following: 




Easy to Apply: Stain typically goes on smoothly, not requiring much precision. It is less likely to drip or streak, making it an exciting choice for DIY enthusiasts. 




Needs Only One Coat: One coat of stain is usually enough to reap the benefits. 




Budget-Friendly: The materials and tools for staining are more affordable than those for painting. 




Highlights Wood’s Natural Beauty: Staining preserves and highlights the beauty of the wood, from cedar and redwood to teak. 




The Cons 




There are drawbacks to consider before staining, such as the following: 




Fading Fast in Sunlight: UV rays eventually break down the stain, causing it to lose its vibrant color and finish. 




Requires Reapplication: Wear and tear can degrade stains faster than paint, so more frequent reapplication may be necessary. 




Less Variety: The range of stain colors and finishes is generally more limited compared to paints. 




In Summary 




Deck staining is ideal for Washington homeowners who want to focus on the allure of wood. For instance, if your deck is made of redwood, it can be impossible to want to cover up its rich, warm reddish-brown hues. The straight and fine grains with knots and swirls are also a stunning visual texture. 




You must not mind sanding, however. Staining a deck means losing just a bit of the natural wood for aesthetics and resilience. 




If your deck is placed in an area where the sun doesn’t shine for long each day, staining can be enough. Sunlight is staining’s weakness; with it in shorter supply, your deck will not sustain much damage. 




The Power of Deck Painting 



Moving on to the latter part of the deck staining vs deck painting battle, Washington homeowners have even more factors to think about. Deck painting involves applying a layer of paint to the surface of your deck, creating a solid, opaque finish that completely covers it. You can go for oil-based, acrylic, latex, or epoxy paint, based on the level of maintenance you are willing to carry out. 




Unlike stains, which go through the decking material, paint sits on top. As such, your deck gets a more robust shield against rot, discoloration, and wear. Paint can also help prevent splinters, with a smooth, even surface for walking and furniture placement. 




Painted decks dramatically transform outdoor spaces. They are not subtle at all, but they are easy to clean, ending the worries that come with wood’s inherent dirt-catching tendencies. 




The Pros 




Why should you choose deck painting over staining? Here are four reasons: 




Long-Lasting: When applied correctly, paint can last several years before requiring touch-ups or reapplication. 

Excellent UV Light Protection: Paint decreases the risk of the wood fading or turning gray because of exposure to sunlight. 

Multiple Color and Finish Options: Whether you prefer bold, vibrant colors or lighter shades, paint has a versatility that stains cannot match. You can also choose from satin, matte, or glossy finishes. 

Better Coverage for Imperfections: Paint hides cracks, blemishes, and age-related wear very well under its layers. 

The Cons 




Here are some potential downsides to using paint: 




More Expensive Than Staining: High-quality exterior paints can be pricey, and you must do more preparation and apply more coats. Maintenance can also be costlier to avoid peeling or chipping. 

Works Best with Professional Service: Proper preparation and application are pivotal for achieving the best results. 

Requires Specific Paint: Decks require exterior-grade paints specifically designed for the materials you are using. 

In Summary 




Perhaps your house is all red bricks, and you crave a shock of all-white, or maybe you have a pool and want to match its cool blue. Deck painting is the only way to go. 




The color of your wood might be astonishing, but if it does not match the rest of your property or your taste, painting over it will give you exactly what you visualize. 




The same solution goes for decks with rough wood surfaces. If staining seeps into cracks and crevices, painting reshapes them in some ways. It hides any unevenness that may be an eyesore. 




Your deck could be in an area where the sun beats down on it all day or one that cannot avoid rain. Regardless, the paint will shield it. 




Deck Staining vs Deck Painting: The Verdict 



With the above perks and pitfalls, it’s easy to see why the deck staining vs deck painting debate has been going on forever. At EA Pro Painters, however, we have a clear winner that we are happy to share with you. 




Deck staining has its place in home improvement, restoration, and other projects, but painting is one step ahead. It has a higher initial price tag, but it certainly delivers. Aside from preserving that natural wood look, painting can generally do everything staining does — and even better. 




Deck painting takes a bit more time and effort, but the results speak for themselves. Plus, with proper upkeep, the investment pays off. At the end of the day, a natural, rustic deck is desirable, but it will not matter if it does not last. 




For superior protection, more aesthetic flexibility, and greater durability, go for deck painting. 




Hire EA Pro Painters for Your Next Decking Project 



EA Pro Painters can provide both deck painting and staining. After all, every house and homeowner in Washington has unique needs. Count on our team to assess your deck and decide which finish it should get, merging your budget and preferences with our expertise. 




As an accredited painting company in the greater Eastside area of King County, we specialize in painting and staining services. Trust us when we say every residence we step into receives professional treatment and the highest quality work. 




Are you ready to get your deck staining or painting project underway? It could be a new construction or a renovation; either way, EA Pro Painters is eager to be on board. Call (206) 250-1194 now or contact us online!

 The Ultimate Guide to Preparing Your Washington Home for Interior Painting 
 April 24, 2025 
 Washington is undeniably a fantastic and beautiful place to live. Who wouldn’t want to make their house look and feel as wonderful as the state itself?  With excellent interior painting, you can bring the beauty and peaceful nature of Washington state inside as a backdrop for your own personal style.  Executing a top-notch interior paint project takes some planning and preparation, though. Whether you live in Bellevue, Woodinville, or Seattle, here are the three steps you should never skip when preparing for interior painting. ﻿ 
 Step 1: Choosing the Right Paint  
Interior painting always begins with the right paint, so put some real thought and consideration into the colors, bases, and finishes.  Colors matter because they influence how you feel within your household and how you perceive each space. For instance, if the purpose of your living room is entertainment, colors like yellow and orange will foster a sense of energy. In contrast, colors like blue and green will bring a restful and soothing atmosphere perfect for bedrooms or bathrooms. When it comes to paint bases, water-based paints like acrylic and latex are the primary choices. Acrylic paints are elastic, clingy, and mildew- and water-resistant, ideal for humid indoor spaces. Similarly, latex paints are quick-drying and easily washable but are more affordable. However, you must be careful during application, as uneven layers produce undesirable finishes. Lastly, paint finishes either absorb or reflect light, creating different textures. If you go for matte paint, you can effectively cover up imperfections. On the other hand, glossy paints may magnify flaws but make spaces look more prominent and brighter. Most homeowners choose eggshell paints, which combine the features of the two finishes.  Selecting Paint Colors That Complement Washington’s Climate – We’re Here to Help  
The paints you choose should not rely solely on your favorite colors or your preferred looks; Washington’s climate is also an essential factor. Consider the long, gloomy months, and hot, dry summers. With these conditions, your interior paint will contribute to your house’s ventilation, lighting, and insulation. For example, those who live in areas with more rainy days than sunshine will benefit from bright shades of glossy paint that keep rooms illuminated. For houses in hot cities, cool colors and matte finishing can help bring the temperature down. At EA Pro Painters, a Washington interior home painter will consider all aspects of your painting project to recommend the best color palettes and finishes.  Step 2: Prepping Your Space for a Professional Finish  
Once you settle on the paint types and color schemes, it is time to prepare your interior. Simply moving furniture farther from the walls to have space to maneuver a brush or roller is not enough; the more well-organized your house is, the faster the painting job will go, and the better the results will be. Start by removing items from the room, from wall hangings to small furniture, and storing them well out of the way. Cover anything you cannot take out, including the floor, with drop cloths.  Next, check your walls for cracks, dents, or holes, and immediately fill them with the proper compounds. Sand them, and once dry, proceed to clean. Dust, dirt, and grime on surfaces will affect how the paint adheres, so be thorough before you get to painting.  Clearing and Protecting Furniture and Floors  
No homeowner wants to deal with damaged furniture and floors after an interior painting project. EA Pro Painters handles the clearing by moving items to designated storage areas, placing big furniture in the center of the room, and covering them to keep them safe. Count on us to use high-quality drop cloths or sheets for floors and save them from potential drips or spills. Washington home interior painting becomes more manageable with every corner of the room freed and safeguarded, leaving the walls and ceilings to get adequate and even coverage, guaranteeing professional-quality results. Upon completing the painting job, we return everything we moved to their original positions, blemish free.  Step 3: Mastering the Priming and Taping Process  
With your interiors ready for painting, priming and taping are the next crucial steps.  Priming before painting provides a uniform base for paint adhesion. One coat should be enough, and two coats of paint will follow.  Taping is all about the corners that are difficult to paint without causing a mess. For instance, if you have intricate trim around your windows, taping will prevent paint from getting where it shouldn’t while the surrounding area still gets a fresh coat.  Expert Taping Tips for Crisp Lines on Edges and Trim  
Even the smallest unpainted spot can ruin the aesthetics of your house. Achieve crisp lines for your edges and trim with these pro tips from EA Pro Painters:  Measure and Mark Points: You can use a pencil to mark all the areas you need to tape and eliminate confusion. A visual guide is always safer than relying on your memory. Use High-Quality Painter’s Tapes: 
 Not all painter’s tape performs the same. Invest in high-quality tapes that stick to surfaces well and easily come off without leaving residue. Press the Tape Firmly: 
 Avoid paint seepage by running a putty knife or other flat object over the tape to seal it tightly onto the surface. Use the Right Brushes or Rollers: Brushes with flagged bristles and multiple lengths will lay down more paint and produce a smoother finish. For more expansive surfaces, rollers of assorted sizes will create consistent layers. Remove While the Paint is Still Slightly Wet: 
 Tapes can peel off dried paint, so remove them at 45-degree angles while the paint is still tacky for clean lines.  
 Final Thoughts  
Washington home interior painting can be the first step toward a truly beautiful house. For the best results, approach your painting project with care and attention to detail.  At EA Pro Painters, we are ready to take over the most challenging parts of interior painting for you, promising a hassle-free and superb painting job. We serve Redmond, Snoqualmie, Everett, and other cities, using our local expertise to enhance your house’s appeal and value. Call (206) 250-1194 or 
contact us online today to get in touch with a professional Washington interior home painter.

Use High-Quality Painter’s Tapes: Not all painter’s tape performs the same. Invest in high-quality tapes that stick to surfaces well and easily come off without leaving residue.

 Top 5 Trending Exterior Paint Colors for Washington Homes in 2025 
 April 24, 2025 
 As a Washington homeowner, you’re no stranger to the area’s natural beauty, especially during the summer and fall seasons. These stunning natural landscapes also provide the perfect backdrop for any property that’s in the state.  Of course, location is just one half of the curb appeal equation. For your Washington home to stand out, you’ll need the right exterior paint to make it pop against Washington’s natural scenery and light.  But what exterior paint colors should you choose? After all, there’s much that the right paint colors can achieve, and choosing the right paint for your property can elevate its ambiance and property value.  Heading deeper into 2025, our EA Pro Painters team sees trends for properties painted in certain shades. So, if you’re stuck for ideas, stick around.  Here are the top five trending exterior paint colors in 2025.  By the end, you’ll have the right inspiration for what colors would look best for your Washington home’s exteriors.   
 Earthly Sage Green  
We kick the list off with an organic classic: earthly sage green.  Earthy sage green is a soft and muted hue that brings a sense of calm and feelings of connection to nature. This color embodies the tranquility of the Pacific Northwest, so it’s the perfect choice if your home is surrounded by lush greenery.  The tone of this shade of green is subtle, allowing any part of your property to blend seamlessly with the natural landscape.  So, if you’re creating a harmonious look that feels both inviting and refreshing, you can’t go wrong with earthly sage green.  Pairing It with Other Colors  
Unless you’re painting your entire home with this color, you’ll need to know what colors complement it. Earthly sage green is an organic and nature-inspired tone, meaning it will go well with neutral tones. In particular, this shade of green matches perfectly with warm neutrals like beige or taupe. Combine them to create a calming effect.  Are you after a more modern look? If you are, crisp whites or soft grays are your best bet. These combinations can create a fresh and clean aesthetic that feels both contemporary and timeless.  How to Use It  
This color works beautifully with a range of styles, so it doesn’t matter if your home is modern or traditional. Earthly sage green is the perfect shade for natural materials like wood and stone. Sage green can also help hide dirt and imperfections, so it’s a practical choice for homes in areas with heavy rainfall or dust — like homes in Puget Sound.  Best Quality: Low Maintenance  
Earthy sage green keeps its beauty over time. It’s no wonder it’s a popular choice among homeowners looking for low-maintenance exterior paint options.  This color tends to show less wear and tear compared to lighter shades, so you won’t have to worry as much about frequent touch-ups.   Warm Neutrals  
Are you up for a more versatile option? If you are, you can’t go wrong with the number two exterior paint color of 2025: warm neutrals.  Warm neutrals are a versatile and inviting choice for any home exterior. These shades include soft beiges, creamy taupes, and gentle browns and create a cozy atmosphere that feels welcoming and timeless.  These color choices serve as a perfect match for various architectural styles and can help your home blend beautifully with Puget Sound’s natural surroundings.  Pairing It with Other Exterior Paint Colors  
So, what do warm neutrals go with? As one of the most versatile paints for 2025, these go with nearly everything.  The possibilities are endless. Warm neutrals work exceptionally well with earthy tones, such as greens (like our number one choice) and browns, and create a harmonious, natural look.  For a more modern twist, you can combine warm neutrals with bold accent colors like deep navy or rich burgundy. This contrast is excellent for adding depth and character to your home’s exterior.  Why They’re a Practical Choice  
Choosing warm neutrals for your exterior paint comes with several practical benefits. These colors are famous for their ability to hide dirt and imperfections, so they’re ideal for homes in areas with heavy rainfall or dust. They also tend to reflect light beautifully, which can help your home feel brighter and more inviting.  Best Quality: Versatility and Timelessness  
Warm neutrals are a timeless choice, meaning they won’t go out of style quickly. This longevity can be a significant advantage when considering resale value because potential buyers often appreciate the classic appeal of these shades.  Deep Charcoal  
There aren’t many simple choices when you’re after a sophisticated exterior. If a bolder and more sophisticated looking home is your goal, choose deep charcoal. Deep charcoal exteriors can add a touch of modern elegance to any home. This rich dark gray hue creates a striking contrast against lighter elements, making it a popular option for homeowners looking to make a statement.   Pairing It with Other Exterior Paint Colors  
When it comes to pairing deep charcoal, the options are both exciting and diverse.  This color looks stunning alongside crisp whites because it can create a dramatic and clean aesthetic. For a more dynamic look, deep charcoal is the perfect match for vibrant colors like mustard yellow or teal.  These bright accents can pop against the dark backdrop and add personality and flair to your home’s exterior.  Practical Considerations  
The best application for deep charcoal is when you’re after sophistication minus the maintenance. This color hides dirt and grime, making it a low-maintenance choice for homeowners.   Best Quality: Modern Aesthetic  
The best quality of deep charcoal is its ability to convey a modern aesthetic. This color exudes sophistication and contemporary style, so it’s a favorite among homeowners who want to create a chic and up-to-date look.  Rich, Leafy Greens  
If Earthy sage green is all about calmness, rich, leafy greens intensify it. Your house will still appear and feel connected to nature, but the boldness and vibrancy take it up a notch. Think of emerald green with deep bluish-green undertones, a rich forest green that reminds you of dense woodlands, or a smooth hunter green with subtle blue undertones. These colors are ideal for those who want more energy and depth for their exterior.   Pairing It with Other Exterior Paint Colors  
Rich, leafy green hues work with neutral and vibrant colors alike. Pair your leafy green with white and beige details for balance, or let yellows, pinks, reds, and blues pop against or complement the backdrop. Grays may also add to the allure of this shade. For nature lovers, brown will never fail to complete the mood you are after.  Potential Challenges  
A darker green paint will be more prone to fading from sunlight, so high-quality materials and maintenance become extra important. Moreover, while green is generally a cool color, richer shades may absorb more heat.  Best Quality: Statement Piece  
No matter what exact hue you go for, rich, leafy green exteriors will always catch the eye. Anyone who gets a glimpse of your house will instantly know that you dare to make a statement and know how to execute it well. Do it right, and your home will stand out for all the right reasons.  Crisp White  
When classic is the look you’re after, look no further than crisp white.  Pristine and elegant, crisp white is a classic choice that brings a fresh and airy ambiance to any home exterior. This color radiates cleanliness and simplicity, so it’s popular among those who desire a bright and inviting atmosphere.  Whether your home features modern lines or traditional details, crisp white enhances your exterior’s architectural elements while serving as a stunning backdrop.  Pairing It with Other Exterior Paint Colors  
There are endless possibilities with crisp white exteriors. Crisp white is compatible with nearly every color, allowing for creative expression in your design choices. And if you’re going for a timeless look, you can pair it with deep navy or charcoal. The combination may seem odd, but it gives you a striking contrast.   Main Practical Consideration: Maintenance  
Versatile and elegant as crisp white is, this exterior paint color can be high maintenance. For this reason, you’ll have to clean painted surfaces regularly to maintain that pristine appearance.   Best Quality: Timeless Elegance  
Whether you’re aiming for a classic look or a modern vibe, crisp white is the perfect foundation for your exterior surfaces. Crisp white is always in vogue, so it’s a wise choice if you’re unsure of what exterior paint color to choose. Because of its versatility, you’ll be able to pair it with an infinite number of paint shades.  A Fresh Coat for Fresher 2025  
There you have it: our picks for the top five trending exterior paint colors for 2025.  These colors are sure to bring out the best in your Puget Sound property, whether it’s your home’s architectural features or its potential as a serene retreat.  But if you still need inspiration and ideas on which color to use on your home, we’re just a call away.  As your Washington exterior home painters, our team at EA Prop Painters offers consultations to help you find the perfect paint color for your property.   Get a fresh new coat for 2025. 
﻿Contact us for a consultation today, and let our pros transform your property’s exterior.

 The Impact of Puget Sound’s Climate on Exterior Paint: How to Choose Weather-Resistant Colors 
 February 4, 2025 
 Living in the Puget Sound area means dealing with a climate that keeps you on your toes. From rainy days to rare summer sunbursts, the weather here is as unpredictable as it is beautiful. ﻿If you’re planning to paint your home’s exterior, the region’s unique climate will challenge you in many ways, particularly when it comes to choosing your paints. Finding the right weather-resistant paint for Puget Sound’s conditions can mean the difference between a long-lasting finish and faded walls that need constant upkeep. In short, the challenges are all too real when you’re choosing paints and colors for your exteriors. Fortunately, we at EA Pro Painters are here to give you actionable tips on finding weather-resistant paints that will last amidst Puget Sound’s unique weather conditions.  
 Understanding Puget Sound’s Climate  
If you’ve lived here for any length of time, you know the drill: There’s plenty of rain, high humidity, and temperatures that can shift dramatically. Summers are mild and often short-lived while winters bring steady moisture and the occasional cold snap. These weather conditions wreak havoc on exterior paint. Excess moisture is a recipe for mold and mildew. Worse yet, temperature fluctuations can cause paint to expand and contract, and that means a lot of cracked surfaces. Don’t underestimate those rare sunny summer days, either. UV rays can still fade colors (especially darker hues) faster than you’d think. Your home’s exterior is in a constant battle with the elements, so you need paint that can last.  Challenges for Exterior Paint in Puget Sound  
Here’s the problem with Puget Sound’s ever-changing weather — it’s relentless. As a result, any attempt to paint your surfaces will come with many weather-related challenges, namely the following.  Moisture-Related Issues  
Rain is a fact of life in Puget Sound. Without the right paint, your home can quickly fall victim to peeling, blistering, and even wood rot. Worse yet, damp conditions (especially 
during the winter) are a breeding ground for mold and mildew, which can turn your beautiful siding into a science experiment.  UV Exposure  
Sun damage may not seem like a big concern here. However, even minimal UV rays can break down pigments and cause colors to fade, leaving your home looking tired.  Temperature Variations and Paint Adhesion  
Your paint is vulnerable to chipping when the weather can’t decide between warm and chilly. Frequent expansion and contraction can cause cracks and weaken adhesion, which makes it easier for water to sneak in.  Selecting Weather-Resistant Paint Colors  
When 
choosing paint types, prioritize quality and formulation since some paints last in changing weather better than others. Acrylic latex paints are likely your best bet because they are 
durable, flexible, and resistant to moisture. These paints can handle temperature swings without cracking, and they’re less prone to mold growth. Now, let’s talk about color. Lighter colors like whites, creams, and soft greys are reflective, helping them hold up better under the sun. Lighter shades also tend to hide dirt and grime better, which is a bonus in our damp climate. Dark colors can work, but you’ll want to choose high-quality pigments designed to resist fading. For instance, blues and greens are classic choices that stay vibrant even in harsh conditions.  Tips for Choosing Durable Exterior Paint Colors  
Here are a few tried and tested tips to help you select the best weather-resistant paints for your exteriors:  Stay Cool: Opt for lighter colors to keep your home cooler and reduce UV damage. Not only does this protect your paint, but it can also help with energy efficiency. Blend In: Earth tones like taupe or sage green complement Puget Sound’s natural beauty, from the lush forests to the misty waterfronts. Think LRV: 
Light Reflectance Value (LRV) is a measure of how much light a color reflects. Higher LRV colors like warm whites and soft yellows are more durable because they absorb less heat and light.  
Popular Weather-Resistant Color Choices for Puget Sound Certain colors just work in this region. When in doubt, go with neutral hues. Neutrals like beige and taupe are timeless and practical. You can also go with blues and greens as they’re inspired by the Pacific Northwest’s waters and forests. For a minimalist look, warm greys and cool whites offer a modern, clean aesthetic.  Proper Application and Maintenance  
Even the best paint won’t last if it’s not applied correctly, which is why you should make sure your walls are clean, dry, and primed before painting. Timing matters, too. Aim to 
paint during the summer season to give the paint plenty of time to cure. Once the paint is on, maintenance is your friend. Regularly cleaning your exterior and inspecting for cracks or peeling can extend the life of your paint job.  Weather-Proof Your Exteriors with the Right Paints (and Professional Painting)  
Choosing and applying high-quality weather-resistant paint and picking durable colors will keep your property looking its best for years to come. But why do the painting yourself when you can leave your project to the pros? At EA Pro Painters, we’ve mastered the art of professional painting in Puget Sound’s climate. From selecting the perfect weather-resistant colors to delivering flawless finishes, we are just a call away in Puget Sound. Visit www.eapropainters.com or give us a call today for a free consultation.

The Impact of Puget Sound’s Climate on Exterior Paint: How to Choose Weather-Resistant Colors
February 4, 2025

Living in the Puget Sound area means dealing with a climate that keeps you on your toes. From rainy days to rare summer sunbursts, the weather here is as unpredictable as it is beautiful. 

﻿

If you’re planning to paint your home’s exterior, the region’s unique climate will challenge you in many ways, particularly when it comes to choosing your paints. Finding the right weather-resistant paint for Puget Sound’s conditions can mean the difference between a long-lasting finish and faded walls that need constant upkeep. 




In short, the challenges are all too real when you’re choosing paints and colors for your exteriors. Fortunately, we at EA Pro Painters are here to give you actionable tips on finding weather-resistant paints that will last amidst Puget Sound’s unique weather conditions. 




Understanding Puget Sound’s Climate 



If you’ve lived here for any length of time, you know the drill: 




There’s plenty of rain, high humidity, and temperatures that can shift dramatically. Summers are mild and often short-lived while winters bring steady moisture and the occasional cold snap. 




These weather conditions wreak havoc on exterior paint. Excess moisture is a recipe for mold and mildew. Worse yet, temperature fluctuations can cause paint to expand and contract, and that means a lot of cracked surfaces. 




Don’t underestimate those rare sunny summer days, either. UV rays can still fade colors (especially darker hues) faster than you’d think. Your home’s exterior is in a constant battle with the elements, so you need paint that can last. 




Challenges for Exterior Paint in Puget Sound 

Here’s the problem with Puget Sound’s ever-changing weather — it’s relentless. As a result, any attempt to paint your surfaces will come with many weather-related challenges, namely the following. 




Moisture-Related Issues 

Rain is a fact of life in Puget Sound. Without the right paint, your home can quickly fall victim to peeling, blistering, and even wood rot. Worse yet, damp conditions (especially during the winter) are a breeding ground for mold and mildew, which can turn your beautiful siding into a science experiment. 




UV Exposure 

Sun damage may not seem like a big concern here. However, even minimal UV rays can break down pigments and cause colors to fade, leaving your home looking tired. 




Temperature Variations and Paint Adhesion 

Your paint is vulnerable to chipping when the weather can’t decide between warm and chilly. Frequent expansion and contraction can cause cracks and weaken adhesion, which makes it easier for water to sneak in. 




Selecting Weather-Resistant Paint Colors 

When choosing paint types, prioritize quality and formulation since some paints last in changing weather better than others. 




Acrylic latex paints are likely your best bet because they are durable, flexible, and resistant to moisture. These paints can handle temperature swings without cracking, and they’re less prone to mold growth. 




Now, let’s talk about color. Lighter colors like whites, creams, and soft greys are reflective, helping them hold up better under the sun. Lighter shades also tend to hide dirt and grime better, which is a bonus in our damp climate. 




Dark colors can work, but you’ll want to choose high-quality pigments designed to resist fading. For instance, blues and greens are classic choices that stay vibrant even in harsh conditions. 




Tips for Choosing Durable Exterior Paint Colors 

Here are a few tried and tested tips to help you select the best weather-resistant paints for your exteriors: 




Stay Cool: Opt for lighter colors to keep your home cooler and reduce UV damage. Not only does this protect your paint, but it can also help with energy efficiency. 
Blend In: Earth tones like taupe or sage green complement Puget Sound’s natural beauty, from the lush forests to the misty waterfronts. 
Think LRV: Light Reflectance Value (LRV) is a measure of how much light a color reflects. Higher LRV colors like warm whites and soft yellows are more durable because they absorb less heat and light. 

Popular Weather-Resistant Color Choices for Puget Sound 

Certain colors just work in this region. When in doubt, go with neutral hues. Neutrals like beige and taupe are timeless and practical. 




You can also go with blues and greens as they’re inspired by the Pacific Northwest’s waters and forests. For a minimalist look, warm greys and cool whites offer a modern, clean aesthetic. 




Proper Application and Maintenance 

Even the best paint won’t last if it’s not applied correctly, which is why you should make sure your walls are clean, dry, and primed before painting. Timing matters, too. Aim to paint during the summer season to give the paint plenty of time to cure. 




Once the paint is on, maintenance is your friend. Regularly cleaning your exterior and inspecting for cracks or peeling can extend the life of your paint job. 




Weather-Proof Your Exteriors with the Right Paints (and Professional Painting) 

Choosing and applying high-quality weather-resistant paint and picking durable colors will keep your property looking its best for years to come. But why do the painting yourself when you can leave your project to the pros? 




At EA Pro Painters, we’ve mastered the art of professional painting in Puget Sound’s climate. From selecting the perfect weather-resistant colors to delivering flawless finishes, we are just a call away in Puget Sound. 




Visit www.eapropainters.com or give us a call today for a free consultation.
